readiness.reason: The release gate relies on static review only. F-007 means the release path can publish without validate. F-001 and F-002 were verified by the lead as security blockers. Engine continuity risks (F-005, F-006) have no synthetic-stream proof.

F-001.reason: Outside engine scope; the lead's static verification is plausible and I did not re-check it.

F-002.reason: Outside engine scope; the lead verified the layer order.

F-003.reason: App supervisor code. The engine worker has no catch_unwind (backend/engine/src/lib.rs:512-577), which is consistent with the concern, but I did not trace the supervisor.

F-005.reason: My own finding. lib.rs:1023-1033 and playout.rs:2337-2347 write filler for the full clip duration after a partial play.

F-006.reason: My own finding. playout.rs:771 and :810 abort on send_packet errors, and the receive_frame loops use is_ok() so other decoder errors are swallowed.

F-012.reason: As worded it overstates the risk. Clip failures return Ok(ClipResult::Fallback) (lib.rs:1018-1036). Err reaches schedule.rs:908 only for output failure or a restart request, where teardown is appropriate.

F-013.reason: clock.rs:51-63 never re-anchors when behind, so the output bursts to catch up after a stall.

F-014.reason: encoded.rs:1330-1334 and :1391-1397 use ? on encoder lookup and open with no software retry. The VAAPI device is hard-wired at :117.

F-015.reason: A stuck reader keeps its permit (live.rs:135-176, :905-918) and the code's own log says a restart may be needed. Severity is uncertain because I did not prove the stuck-syscall case.

F-016.reason: Real behaviour at scte35.rs:847-856 and :423: one corrupt TS packet disables signalling. Severity is LOW.

F-025.reason: No synthetic-stream tests exist for live reconnect, mid-clip failure fallback or encoder-open failure paths. The SCTE-35 unit tests are good, but I saw no end-to-end test.

F-035.reason: Setup and deployment scope; not reviewed.
